## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Pajahanavāra* is a section of the *Yamaka*, the sixth book of the Theravāda Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. In the overall architecture of the *Anusayayamaka* (the chapter on underlying tendencies or biases), the *Pajahanavāra* constitutes the third subdivision, treating the topic of "abandoning the biases" (*pajahana-vāra*) [Nyanatiloka 2007]. It immediately follows the treatment of being possessed of biases (*sānusaya-vāra*) and precedes the section on full penetration (*pariññā-vāra*), alongside other sections examining abandoned biases (*pahīna-vāra*), their arising (*uppajjana-vāra*), and their relation to the planes of existence (*dhātu-vāra*) [Nyanatiloka 2007]. SuttaCentral records one modern translation of this section into a modern language [SuttaCentral].

No direct external parallels are recorded for the text on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral]. Computational analysis by DharmaNexus indicates extensive formulaic text reuse within the Pali Abhidhamma tradition, matching 24,989 passages across 57 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The closest textual alignments occur with adjacent and structural partner sections of the *Yamaka*, most heavily the *Pariññāvāra* (Ya 7.2.4) and *Sānusayavāra* (Ya 7.2.2), as well as the *Anusayavāra* (Ya 7.2.1), *Uppajjanavāra* (Ya 7.2.6), and sections of the *Indriyayamaka* (Ya 10) [DharmaNexus]. Significant reuse is also identified in the commentary (*Pañcapakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā*) and subcommentaries (*Pañcapakaraṇa-mūlaṭīkā* and *anuṭīkā*) [DharmaNexus]. Across languages, DharmaNexus automatically aligns passages of the text with Northern Buddhist Abhidharma and Yogācāra treatises treating related psychological categories, such as the Tibetan translations of the *Abhidharmakośabhāṣya* and *Abhidharmasamuccayavyākhyā*, as well as Sanskrit texts including Harivarman's *Satyasiddhiśāstra* and the *Yogācārabhūmi* [DharmaNexus].
